DNS protection

Filter bypass

Off

Unblocks sites your network filters by the site name (like YouTube Restricted Mode) — no VPN, full speed. Works with Chromium-family browsers.

Apps

App tunnel

Sends only the apps you launch from here through a WireGuard tunnel. The rest of the machine keeps its normal connection and speed. If the tunnel drops, those apps lose connectivity instead of silently falling back.

Diagnose a domain

Resolves each domain through your network's resolver and through DoH, probes every address returned, and flags forced content restriction (such as YouTube Restricted Mode). Tells you whether a problem is DNS before you change anything.

Profiles optional

You don't need any. Protection already covers every site and app. A profile is for forcing specific domains over DoH when you narrow the default policy, or for a one-click launch command.

A leading *. matches subdomains only. Only add domains you have actually observed.

DoH providers

Tried top to bottom — if one fails or is blocked, the next one answers. Keep at least two from different companies.

Add a custom provider

The provider's own IP addresses, so reaching it never depends on DNS.

Domain rules

A domain covers its subdomains; a leading *. means subdomains only. .local, .lan, home.arpa, single-word names and private-address reverse lookups already stay local. Use the right-hand list for campus or company sites that only resolve on your network.

Updates Checking…
What needs your password, and why. DNS protection and the app tunnel ask through polkit: binding port 53, writing /etc/resolv.conf, and creating a network interface all require root. The original resolver file is backed up first and restored when you stop. If the helper is killed, the next start restores it before anything else.
